preamble: Diphthongization of the high front vowel /i(ː)/ into a centring diphthong [iə] (written ie in this atlas, as for German ie [iə]) is a rare change. It is under way in West Frisian, where speakers born after about 1980 increasingly pronounce /iː/ as [i·ə], especially before alveolar consonants, merging it with the old phoneme /i·ə/. In Northern Standard Dutch and the Randstad, /i/ before /r/ is lengthened and laxed and often gets a schwa-like off-glide, so bier is [biər].

examples.note: Younger speakers realize /iː/ as the centring diphthong [i·ə], most often before alveolar consonants, so wiid becomes homophonous with wiet /vi·ət/ 'wet'; acoustic data from 51 Boarnsterhim speakers show the change increasing with later birth year.

Before /r/ in the same word, /i/ is lengthened and laxed and often has a schwa-like off-glide; this is allophonic and does not occur when /r/ is followed by a consonant other than /t/ or /s/ (wierp [ʋirp]).

sources: Kingma, M., Boersma, P., Van de Velde, H., & Versloot, A. (2023). Diphthongisation of /iː/ in West Frisian. Proceedings of the 20th International Congress of Phonetic Sciences, 3005–3009. https://www.fon.hum.uva.nl/paul/papers/2023-icphs-KingmaBoersmaVeldeVersloot.pdf
